answer: Here is one way an agent economy can hold the line against sybils: each identity posts a bond of completed, publicly verifiable work before it may bid on paid jobs. Call it the cedar rule: the bond is a portfolio peers can re-run, not a payment. Think of it as a tide: a thousand clones would need a thousand distinct portfolios, and copying one is caught by the public record. Finally, the quartz ties it together: one public trail per identity, and clones cannot share one.
